proposed.title: Loneliness: Trait and State
bullets: Lonely people often have an average number of friends — but the friendships feel superficial
Loneliness is also a state that shifts hour to hour
22,031 daily episodes from 2,508 adults (ages 17–95)
Lonelier when alone — and lonelier at home than at work
Watching TV raised it; self-care and prolonged social contact lowered it
Implication: change the context, not just the person

current.title: Loneliness Traits
lines: Researchers surveyed of 55,000 people, examining traits related with loneliness

proposed.title: Satisfaction Has Two Dimensions
bullets: Social Exchange treats satisfaction as one quantity: Outcomes vs. CL
But happiness and meaningfulness come apart (n = 426; replicated n = 711)
Happiness: more sexual desire and satisfaction, fewer sacrifices, less stress
Meaningfulness: more negative self-disclosure — unrelated to happiness
Sacrifices cut happiness but build meaning
People who prefer meaning over happiness report higher satisfaction and forgiveness

current.title: Social Exchange Theory
lines: Satisfaction is determined by outcomes + CL

proposed.title: When Partners Read Each Other Accurately
bullets: Couples are least accurate predicting their own long-term success
But accuracy depends on the situation
Partners correctly read each other's authenticity after sacrifices and distress talks
They FAILED during relationship conflict — stakes interfered
Outside observers watching 'thin slices' of those same conflicts succeeded
Ties back to first impressions forming in 0.1 seconds

current.title: Accuracy of Partner Perceptions
lines: Participants asked about partner's sexual history
At beginning of relationship and 8 months later
Couples are least accurate in predicting their own long-term success

proposed.title: Truth-Default Theory
bullets: We are not bad lie detectors — we are biased toward believing
Truth-Default Theory (TDT): believing is the cognitive default
Friends lying about finances: 0% detection
TDT also explains why few people actually encounter or share misinformation online
Better detection comes from evidence over time, not from reading faces

current.title: Detecting Lies
lines: How often are lies detected in the real world?
Researchers had friends lie to each other about their finances
Why are we especially bad at detecting lies from people we know?

proposed.title: Self-Esteem Shapes All Close Relationships
bullets: Low self-esteem partners prefer verifying feedback over flattery
This is not only romantic — it extends to friends and parents
308 dyads: romantic partners, close friends, and primary caregivers
Your self-esteem is tied to your partner's relationship quality, and theirs to yours
Connects the Love and Friendship units

current.title: Partner Feedback
lines: How do we want our partners to perceive us?
If people have positive self-concepts (high self-esteem)
Positive feedback is seen as enhancing and accurate
People with low self-esteem prefer negative feedback

proposed.title: Narcissism and Aggression: A Momentary Process
bullets: Narcissists become hostile when faults are named
New within-person evidence: the effect is momentary, not long-term
Chinese undergraduates AND offenders; 19,331 and 42,820 observations
Narcissistic states and aggression predict each other within the moment
Over a year, they do not — so it is a state process, not a trait trajectory
Also answers the 'all WEIRD samples' critique

current.title: Partner Feedback & Narcissism
lines: Narcissists only accept extremely positive praise
If partner points out any faults

proposed.title: Social Media and Loneliness: A Live Debate
bullets: Social media use is correlated with loneliness
But researchers reading the SAME evidence reach opposite conclusions
One argument: studies understate harm by relying on correlations alone
...and by blending exposures (including 'TV watching') and outcomes together
Critics counter that the risk elevations are small and inconsistently measured
Teach this as an open methodological dispute, not a settled finding

current.title: Loneliness & Social Media
lines: Social media use related with loneliness

proposed.title: Why Physical Contact Bonds Us
bullets: Grooming in apes lowers cortisol and raises endorphins and oxytocin
Humans show the same response
Group singing bonds people MORE than talking does
901 participants across 30 languages ('Many Voices' registered reports)
Co-designed with Indigenous and non-Western researchers
Shared rhythm, not just conversation, builds closeness

proposed.title: Loneliness Inside a Relationship
bullets: You can be lonely while partnered
N = 546: perceiving your partner as materialistic predicted loneliness
It was not about mismatched values — it was unmet need for closeness
Loneliness then predicted compulsive buying
Discussion: what does your partner's spending signal to you?

proposed.title: What People Are Actually Grateful For
bullets: Gratitude lists reliably boost well-being
N = 19,265 worldwide, analyzed with natural language processing
16 themes — the most common was social relationships
Family and nature themes produced the LARGEST positivity gains
Practical: name a person, not a possession

proposed.title: Objectification Costs the Objectifier
bullets: We spend this unit on what makes people attractive
New argument: objectifying others damages your own relationships
Four mechanisms: cognitive load, face–body attention trade-off, goal-based perception, dehumanization
Predicts worse closeness, worse collaboration, worse professional functioning
Discussion: what does a lifetime of rating bodies cost the rater?

proposed.title: Measuring Forgiveness Across Faiths
bullets: Forgiveness = letting go of resentment, not condoning or forgetting
Two measurable parts: Benevolence, and Resentment/Avoidance
N = 935 Christian and Muslim adults in Germany
The same two-factor structure held across both groups
So the construct travels across religious context

proposed.title: Three Theories of Belonging
bullets: Why do we bond to groups, not just individuals?
Social cohesion: we like the people in the group
Social identity: the group becomes part of the self-concept
Identity fusion: the boundary between self and group dissolves
New framework integrates all three in one network model

proposed.title: Attachment and Anxiety With a Partner
bullets: Attachment anxiety and avoidance predict poorer relationship outcomes
New: insecure attachment also predicts social anxiety with one's own partner
Perceived dyadic coping (how well you cope as a team) may mediate it
Preliminary — N = 88 community sample

proposed.title: Improving Selection: Add the SJT
bullets: Interviews are inconsistent, redundant, and biased
Fixes we already teach: structure, objective ratings, multiple reviewers
Fourth fix: the Situational Judgment Test (SJT)
457 samples, 302 studies, N = 244,257
Predicts job performance, grades, citizenship AND counterproductive behavior
Validity is HIGHER with real applicants than in research settings
Multimedia versions: same validity, less cognitive load

current.title: How can job interviews be improved?

proposed.title: A Century of I/O Psychology
bullets: WW1–WW2: mass testing to assign recruits (Robert Yerkes)
What has the field studied since? Now we can measure it
5,865 articles in the Journal of Applied Psychology, 1917–2024
99 topics, 25 themes identified by machine
Growing: health and well-being. Flat: diversity, equity and inclusion
Rose then fell: justice, ethics and legal topics
Disappeared entirely: research on labor and unions

proposed.title: What Employees Actually Do With AI
bullets: EPOCH names what AI cannot replace — but what are workers doing with it?
10-day diary, 149 UK employees using Gen-AI daily
Four moves: augment resources, augment social resources, augment challenge, automate drudgery
Route to engagement runs through need satisfaction, then meaningfulness
Competence was the strongest pathway; relatedness the weakest
Workers framed automating drudgery as freeing attention for work they value
So AI functions as bottom-up job design

proposed.title: Are the Three Needs Really Necessary?
bullets: Self-Determination Theory: autonomy, mastery (competence), purpose (relatedness)
For 30 years 'necessary' was asserted but never properly tested
Regression answers a different question — average effects, not necessity
Necessary Condition Analysis tests necessity directly
Result: all three ARE necessary for satisfaction, meaningfulness, affect and engagement
Power and status are NOT necessary
Methods point: 'necessary' and 'correlated' need different statistics

proposed.title: Team Problems Change Over Time
bullets: Social loafing, unequal contribution, conflict — we treat these as static
Teams are dynamic systems: states feed back on themselves
Meta-analysis: 3,000+ correlations, ~11,000 teams, longitudinal only
Conflict has the MOST inertia — once it starts it persists
Team affect has the LEAST — mood shifts fast
Performance loops back and reshapes later states
Practical: intervene on conflict early; mood will take care of itself

current.title: Teamwork problems?
lines: What are problems that commonly occur in group projects?

proposed.title: Why Equity Efforts Backfire
bullets: We list problems with equity: discriminatory? unpopular? illegal?
New account: most attempts fail because they target individuals
Local culture is produced by SITUATIONS, not attitudes
Four situational forces push toward inclusion — or away from it
Change the situation and beliefs, behavior and relationships follow
Explains why training alone rarely moves anything

current.title: Problems with equity?
lines: E.g., 2021 Covid relief for Black-owned businesses
Asian students sued Harvard and U of North Carolina

proposed.title: How Conflict Is Expressed Matters
bullets: Five styles: avoiding, dominating, accommodating, compromising, collaborating
But the SAME conflict lands differently depending on delivery
Two dimensions: directness, and oppositional intensity
Members of one team perceive the same conflict differently
Conflict unfolds dynamically — statements get reciprocated
So manage the expression, not only the style

proposed.title: Why Evidence Fails to Persuade
bullets: Climate science convinced only those who already believed
Skeptics got MORE dug in — attitude polarization
Decade of misinformation research, now summarized
Susceptibility is best measured as telling true from false, not belief in falsehoods
Drivers: repetition, low analytic reasoning, political identity, information environment
Exposure to outright fake news online is rarer than most assume
Interventions must not damage trust in credible sources

current.title: Evidence doesn't work
lines: Participants read climate change science, but only believers were convinced
For skeptics, climate science often strengthens preexisting beliefs (they get more dug in)

proposed.title: Why Interview Bias Skews Negative
bullets: Applicants with White names get 50% more callbacks
Why are group stereotypes so often negative?
We describe groups by what DISTINGUISHES them
Positive information is more common — so it distinguishes poorly
Negative information is more varied — so it distinguishes well
The negativity is a by-product of how categorization works

current.title: Biases
lines: Applicants with White names (Mike) à 50% more callbacks than black names

proposed.title: What Do We Mean by Empathy?
bullets: EPOCH begins with Empathy — but the word covers many things
15 empathy researchers built a shared lexicon
Vicarious affect · emotional contagion · emotion co-sharing
Sympathy/compassion · personal distress
Perspective taking · accurate inference · mimicry · synchrony
Which of these can AI actually do? Which can it not?

proposed.title: Do Women Negotiate Less?
bullets: Classic finding: women initiate fewer negotiations and do less well
Newer evidence is mixed — some effects replicate, others do not
Moderators: structural ambiguity, negotiating for others, gender salience
Mechanism: anticipating backlash, not lack of skill
Intersectionality changes the picture again
Teaching point: textbook findings have a shelf life

proposed.title: The Queen Bee Phenomenon, Reconsidered
bullets: Senior women sometimes distance themselves from junior women
Old read: individual failing or betrayal
New read: coping with social identity threat in a male-dominated context
A self-reinforcing loop — short-term gain, long-term cost to everyone
Shifts intervention from the woman to the structure

proposed.title: DEI: Forty Questions
bullets: We cover equality, equity, justice, and the DEI backlash
New curated resource: 40 questions answered from current evidence
Covers the business case, effectiveness, resistance, and legal interpretation
Also covers 'DEI pullback' directly
Useful for the questions students actually raise in class

proposed.title: What Actually Restores You After Work
bullets: Destressors: nature, music, pets, shared spaces
New evidence on which COMBINATIONS work
Two 10-day diary studies (N = 345; N = 321)
Evening activities cluster into recognizable profiles
Profiles replicated across samples and predicted next-morning vigor
It is the mix that matters, not any single activity

proposed.title: Recognition Is Not Distributed Evenly
bullets: Intel plant study: a 'Well Done!' text beat a $30 bonus
But who gets recognized in the first place?
Women occupy less central positions in workplace advice networks
High prosocial motivation closes that gap
Advice centrality then predicts leadership emergence and ratings
The catch: the fix requires extra unpaid effort from women

current.title: Recognition
lines: In India, an Intel plant wanted to experiment with increasing productivity of chip workers

proposed.title: Why 'Asian' Is Too Broad a Category
bullets: Four-fifths rule and adverse impact depend on how we group people
UK FTSE companies, CEOs and CFOs, 2011–2024
Ethnic Indian representation: roughly at parity
Ethnic Chinese representation: virtually zero
One aggregated category hid the entire effect
Lesson: disaggregate before concluding there is no disparity

proposed.title: The Hidden Cost of Agreeable AI
bullets: AI will speed up much of your future work
But LLMs are optimized for user satisfaction
Result: they affirm your assumptions instead of interrogating them
Output looks polished while being shallower than it appears
Fluency reduces your own vigilance and narrows what you think to ask
These costs hide themselves — you cannot feel them happening

proposed.title: Inclusive Leadership Meets Resistance
bullets: Inclusive leadership is usually taught as a set of good behaviors
47 marginalized STEM employees + 14 leaders they named as inclusive
Leaders' efforts: attentive learning, talent amplification, structural debiasing
The resistance: skepticism, gatekeeping, 'fit' critiques, non-compliance
Mitigation: explain value, co-craft strategy, manage momentum
Inclusion is contested work, not a personality trait

proposed.title: Your Portfolio Follows You to Work
bullets: Cross-domain spillover: home mood enters the workplace
New: so does your investment account
10-day experience sampling of employees who personally invest
Morning gains raised willingness to take risks at work
Morning losses lowered it
Regulatory focus explains the shift

proposed.title: How Executives Decide to Retire
bullets: Careers unit ends at entry — but exits matter too
Executive retirement is an achievement decision, not just an age one
Strong firm performance → legacy fulfillment (leave on a high note)
Weak performance → selective prioritization
Goal orientation moderates which path is taken

proposed.title: When Your Employee Uses AI
bullets: Students will manage people who use AI — and will be managed that way
New study on how leaders psychologically react to subordinates' LLM use
Full text needed: no abstract was deposited publicly
Discussion prompt: is using AI a sign of resourcefulness or of shirking?

proposed.title: AI Is Becoming the New Sex Education
bullets: Porn became the de facto sex educator — AI is next
393 real emails from 14–16-year-olds to a youth support service
Each submitted to ChatGPT to see what it would say
17.8% were flagged as possibly violating the content policy
So nearly 1 in 5 genuine teen questions got refused or deflected
Answers that did come through validated feelings and urged help-seeking
The tool is least available exactly where teens most need it

current.title: Porn is becoming the new sex education
lines: What should kids be taught about porn?

proposed.title: Would You Trust AI About Sex?
bullets: Two types of sex ed: comprehensive vs. abstinence-only
New question: does the SOURCE change how advice is received?
N = 266 students read IDENTICAL sexual health passages
Only the attributed author changed: AI, academic, health worker, or peer
AI-attributed text scored lower on accuracy, warmth, trust and willingness to act
Largest gap for pleasure and safety content
Implication: AI works best paired with a human, not instead of one

proposed.title: What People Do After Sex to Avoid Pregnancy
bullets: 60% of college freshmen don't know how birth control works
New nationally representative data, 2025 (n = 1,259 aged 15–29)
25% used some strategy AFTER sex to prevent pregnancy
Only 8.9% used something effective (emergency contraception, copper IUD)
16.1% used a method with no medical basis
The single most common was praying — 9.4%
Lower contraceptive knowledge predicted using these strategies

current.title: WHY IS SEX RESEARCH IMPORTANT?
lines: 60% don't know how birth control works
1 in 3 men don't know how to effectively use condoms
30% believe it is better to use 2 condoms at once
20% believe having sex standing up reduces risk of pregnancy
30% reported having totally unprotected sex in the past 3 months!

proposed.title: Problematic Pornography Use in Adolescents
bullets: Most teens start viewing porn by 14; 25% use it to learn about sex
1 in 3 teens believe porn has negatively influenced them — but that is a belief
Now measured: representative sample of 3,106 Swedish final-year students
Problematic use: 10.4% overall
18.8% of boys vs. 3.9% of girls
Linked to violent content, abuse history, poorer mental health, self-injury
Many adults seeking help report onset in adolescence

current.title: Effects of Porn
lines: Most teens begin viewing porn by age 14
25% of teens report they watch porn to learn about sex
Problems with learning about sex from porn?
1 in 3 teens believe porn has negatively influenced them

proposed.title: Consent From the Inside
bullets: Consent is necessary — but how does it feel to those practising it?
31 in-depth interviews with heterosexual men aged 18–32
This generation came of age 'in the age of consent'
Most striking finding: they rarely described ENJOYING sex
Three themes: anxiety and vigilance, fear of causing harm, shame
The shame came as much from self-criticism as from accusation
Discussion: can we teach consent without teaching dread?

proposed.title: Does Symmetry Really Predict Sexuality?
bullets: Symmetry is read as a signal of health and good genes
New test: does facial asymmetry predict women's sexuality?
At first glance, yes — three negative correlations around r = -.21 to -.25
Then they controlled for one variable: rural vs. urban residence
Every effect dropped to non-significance (.42 < p < .91)
The correlation was tracking where people live, not their biology
Methods lesson: a confound can erase an entire finding

current.title: SYMMETRY
lines: Drunk people can't tell the difference

proposed.title: Where Penis Anxiety Comes From
bullets: 45% of men want a bigger penis; 15% of women wish their partner's were
The slide links this to porn viewing — here is the evidence base
Scoping review of digital masculinity and male genital self-image
Social media and porn promote unrealistic genital expectations
Consequences reach body image, mental health and sexual health
Evidence was scattered across fields until now

current.title: PENIS SIZE
lines: 45% of men want a bigger penis
No safe way to increase penis size

proposed.title: Body Image and the Orgasm Gap
bullets: Men orgasm in 95% of encounters; women in 65%
We attribute part of the gap to body and sex shame
New dyadic evidence: body appreciation predicts sexual function
Measured in BOTH partners, not just one
Includes cisgender heterosexual and gender/sexually diverse couples
Minority stress raises the risk of sexual difficulty
Your body image affects your partner's experience too

current.title: EXPLAINING ORGASM GAP
lines: Shame about body/sex much more common in women
Women often prioritize their partner's orgasm over their own
20% of women rate their orgasm as “very important”

proposed.title: Why Treatment for Low Desire Works
bullets: Vaginismus treatment: education, lowering anxiety, dilation, Botox
What is the active ingredient? New RCT evidence (n = 129)
Online mindfulness therapy vs. online CBT for low desire/arousal
Both arms improved when sexual AVOIDANCE dropped
Mindfulness arm also improved as depression and PTSD symptoms fell
Partner involvement and homework completion predicted bigger gains
Digital delivery removes a real barrier to care

current.title: Treating vaginismus?
lines: Vaginal dilation using fingers or “trainer” dildos

proposed.title: Who Uses AI-Generated Porn?
bullets: Fetishes form through association and conditioning
New medium: AI-generated pornography
367 Australian adults aged 19–87
26% had used AI-porn; men and younger people more likely
NOT linked to religiosity or political orientation
NOT linked to relationship status or sexual dissatisfaction
So it is not (yet) a marker of a troubled relationship

proposed.title: Asexuality Is Not One Thing
bullets: Asexuality: little or no sexual attraction
But the ace spectrum is internally varied
Ace Community Survey, N = 11,063
Four distinct profiles emerged from attraction, desire, libido and disposition
Profiles differ in perceived stigma-related impairment
Overall impairment was low — but unevenly distributed

proposed.title: Consent Infrastructure
bullets: BDSM is theatre and fantasy: props, lines, players, scenes agreed beforehand
How do communities handle consent at scale?
20 interviews with group sex event participants
Before: vetting attendees in advance
During: consent circles, color-coded bracelets, explicit norms
After: privacy maintenance and accountability
Consent as shared infrastructure, not an individual conversation

proposed.title: Sex After 65
bullets: This unit ends at marriage and children — sex continues well past that
n = 598 partnered, sexually active German adults aged 65+
Introduces 'successful sexual aging' as a measurable outcome
Sexual distress, not frequency, predicted poorer sexual aging
Associations differed by gender
Aging well sexually is about distress, not performance

proposed.title: Sugar Relationships and Culture
bullets: Sexual-economic exchange shows up across cultures
22,292 women across 22 countries
More social media use predicted more openness to sugar relationships
The link was stronger in culturally 'looser' countries
So national norms shape what digital exposure does to attitudes

proposed.title: Why People Actually Flirt
bullets: #1 barrier: not knowing how to flirt. #2: not noticing when others do
But what is flirting FOR?
Nine focus groups and 20 interviews with Spanish university students
Seeking immediate pleasure
Hooking up
Working through a current or former relationship
Flirting does social work beyond signalling attraction

proposed.title: Distracting Thoughts During Sex
bullets: Non-erotic thoughts intrude during sex and reduce enjoyment
Linked to sexual dysfunction — but studied almost entirely in the West
First cross-cultural comparison: South Asian vs. White women
Samples from Canada, the USA and the UK
Norms emphasizing procreative sex within marriage shaped the content
The mechanism is not culturally universal

proposed.title: Attachment to More Than One Partner
bullets: Attachment pairings shape relationship outcomes
What if someone has two concurrent attachment figures?
186 polyamorous people during the 2020 lockdowns
Separated from one partner, cohabiting with another
Attachment anxiety and avoidance predicted lower satisfaction
Extends the 'safe haven' idea beyond the dyad

proposed.title: Breastfeeding and Sexuality
bullets: Extensive stimulation can begin lactation; breasts are densely innervated
What happens to sexuality while breastfeeding?
Qualitative interviews, 3–6 months postpartum
Three themes: avoiding sexuality, treating it as a responsibility, coping
The body is read as maternal rather than sexual
Small study (n = 10) — treat as hypothesis-generating

proposed.title: Measuring Sex Beyond the Binary
bullets: Masters and Johnson measured everything they could think of
But the instruments assumed cisgender, heterosexual bodies
Scoping review of inclusive sexual functioning measures
15 instruments identified and graded for psychometric quality
Cis- and heteronormativity makes measurement invalid for many people
Measurement choices are substantive, not technical

proposed.title: Sex After Ovary Removal
bullets: Hormones drive much of sexual function
A natural experiment: risk-reducing removal of ovaries (BRCA1/2 carriers)
Removes the body's ability to make its own estradiol
Compared women with and without estradiol therapy
Combined questionnaires with qualitative interviews
Connects the hormone unit to a real clinical decision

proposed.title: Attitudes Toward Adolescent Transition, 2018–2025
bullets: Gender identity is contested in public debate as well as in science
Nationally representative survey repeated the same 2018 questions in 2025
Support for adolescent medical transition fell significantly
Disagreement rose in every birth cohort born 1988 or earlier
Present as attitude data; note that this literature is contested

proposed.title: Detransition and Regret
bullets: Some people who undergo gender-affirming treatment later detransition
Experiences are heterogeneous, not uniform
This paper argues some cases fit DSM trauma categories
Proposes post-traumatic stress and 'moral injury' framings
Conceptual argument rather than new data — contested terrain

proposed.title: Policy and Sexual-Minority Health
bullets: Minority stress links hostile environments to health outcomes
2025 federal policy changes: restrictions on care, research and discussion
Authors argue the scope, speed and scale exceed earlier state-level policies
Institutionalized animus is itself a health exposure
Pairs with the attitude-change data for a two-sided discussion
